headline: State desk: Michigan tax portal opens; Vermont event sales near
dek: Michigan moved its cannabis taxes to a new portal on 12 November, Vermont takes event-sale bids from 16 November, and Illinois Zen Leaf staff dropped their union.
key_points: From 7:00 on 12 November, Michigan businesses can register, file and pay the new wholesale marijuana tax and the retail excise tax in the MiTreasury eServices business portal.
All 2026 quarterly wholesale marijuana tax returns are due on 20 January 2027, and retail excise returns filed after 30 October must be filed separately for each licence number.
Vermont retailers can apply to sell at approved events from 16 to 30 November, with a lottery on 16 December; consumption on site stays banned.
Workers at an Illinois Zen Leaf dispensary, a Verano brand, voted 10-1 to decertify UFCW Local 881, and the NLRB certified the result on 3 November.
body: Three states, three practical changes for licensed operators. Michigan's cannabis taxes moved to a new state portal this morning after a filing blackout of up to two weeks. Vermont is days away from taking applications for a pilot that lets retailers sell at concerts, fairs and other events. And in Illinois, workers at a Zen Leaf dispensary have voted their union out, the latest in a string of decertifications in the cannabis trade.

None of these is a headline policy shift on its own. Together they show where the work in state markets is right now: tax administration, new sales channels for small businesses, and labour relations in an industry where some states tie licences to union agreements.
## Michigan: both cannabis taxes move online

At 7:00 on 12 November, Michigan's Department of Treasury switched on full support for its wholesale marijuana tax in the MiTreasury eServices business portal. Taxpayers and their preparers can now register for the tax, file and pay returns, update account details and message the Treasury directly. The wholesale tax had been unavailable in eServices from 4 to 11 November, so no payments could be made that week. The Treasury tells businesses to register the CRA licence number for each location liable for the tax, using the same numbers they directed quarterly payments to in the first three quarters of 2026. All 2026 quarterly returns for the wholesale tax are due on 20 January 2027.

The retail marijuana excise tax moved on the same day, from the older Michigan Treasury Online system to the same new portal. That tax was offline on every platform from 17:00 on 30 October until this morning, and the Treasury warned that returns and payments filed late during the blackout could draw penalties and interest. There is also a change in how the tax is reported: until now, excise returns were filed by location, but any tax period filed after 30 October must be filed separately for each licence number, so a store with several licences will file several returns. Account links created in the old system do not carry over, and the Treasury advises keeping a copy of the most recent return to reconnect.
> Michigan is now collecting two cannabis taxes through one new portal, and the first deadline that tests it is 20 January.
## Vermont: retail sales at events, without consumption

Vermont's Cannabis Control Board will begin accepting applications for cannabis event permits on 16 November, Marijuana Moment reported. Under the pilot, licensed retailers can apply between 16 and 30 November, and the board will hold regional lotteries on 16 December to pick which retailers can go on to seek permits for specific events, according to The Marijuana Herald. Sales would take place in a sanctioned area at an approved event, but buyers could not consume on site.

The pilot is aimed at a market built on small growers. About 300 Vermont cultivators farm 1,000 square feet or less, WCAX reported in October, and many cannot afford a storefront. Board chair James Pepper told the station the Legislature wants more retailers to be able to bring products to residents and visitors, while the state held back on consumption rules over safety concerns. Retailers told WCAX that events would help them reach customers in a state with strict advertising limits.
## Illinois: Zen Leaf workers vote out their union

Employees at an Illinois Zen Leaf dispensary voted 10-1 on 26 October to remove United Food and Commercial Workers Local 881 as their bargaining representative, and the National Labor Relations Board certified the result on 3 November, according to a release from the National Right to Work Foundation published by Cannabis Business Times. The petition was filed by employee Elias Driscoll with free legal help from the foundation's lawyers. Zen Leaf is the retail brand of Chicago-based Verano Holdings. MetaFlora did not find a public response from the union.

The foundation, which opposes compulsory union fees, says cannabis workers in New Jersey, Ohio, Massachusetts and Missouri have also won decertification votes with its help. It argues that Illinois gives preference in licensing to dispensaries with labour peace agreements and wants the NLRB to act against state laws that require them. Those claims come from an advocacy group, but the policy point is real for operators: in several states, the licence process and the union question are linked.

In Michigan, the first full filing cycle in the new portal ends with the 20 January 2027 deadline for 2026 wholesale tax returns. In Vermont, the application window runs from 16 to 30 November, followed by the 16 December lottery. And in labour, watch whether other Illinois dispensaries with labour peace agreements see similar petitions, and whether the NLRB takes up the foundation's challenge to state union mandates.
